principles: Current host terminology must match the user-visible product: Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI, Antigravity CLI.
Legacy compatibility must be explicit and bounded, never advertised as the preferred current path.
Host runtime changes must preserve conservative unattended-safety semantics and dispatch gates.
Verification should prove both the new agy path and non-regression for legacy records.
drivers: Antigravity/agy is installed locally but rejected by Lattice host_runtime_probe.
Existing code and docs still present Gemini as a current host.
Multi-host development needs Lattice to recognize all current host宿主 before relying on them.

options.name: A: Add antigravity as first-class host and keep gemini as deprecated legacy alias/id
pros: Unblocks agy immediately without breaking older records or tests that mention gemini.
Lets docs and current lists move to Antigravity while legacy behavior remains inspectable.
Smallest safe runtime change for a first development slice.
cons: Some legacy gemini code remains and needs clear deprecated labeling.
A later cleanup story may still be needed if the user wants hard deletion of every gemini surface.

options.name: B: Replace gemini entirely with antigravity and remove all gemini host handling now
pros: Strongest semantic cleanup and no lingering old third-host name.
Simpler current host list after removal.
cons: Higher compatibility risk for existing dispatch records, policies, docs, and tests.
Broader blast radius inside dispatch and usage-ledger provider code.
Could derail the requested cli-engine split by turning this into a breaking migration.

options.name: C: Only update docs and leave runtime host ids unchanged
pros: Very small change and low code risk.
cons: Does not solve the real failure: host_runtime_probe rejects antigravity.
Would mislead multi-host development because agy still cannot be selected through Lattice.

chosen: A: Add antigravity as first-class host and keep gemini as deprecated legacy alias/id
rationale: Choose A because it makes Antigravity/agy usable now, aligns current user-facing host semantics, and avoids a breaking removal of legacy Gemini records during the first enabling story.

preMortem.scenario: Antigravity is added to probe but dispatch policy still rejects it
preMortem.trigger: KNOWN_HOSTS or allowed host validation remains hard-coded to fake/claude-code/gemini/codex
preMortem.consequence: User sees probe pass but cannot use Antigravity in policy or dispatch flows
preMortem.mitigation: Update dispatch-policy known hosts and run policy/probe smoke checks.

preMortem.scenario: Docs still teach Gemini as the current third host
preMortem.consequence: Users pick the deprecated command and the new agy support feels inconsistent
preMortem.mitigation: Update current-host prose and examples to Codex, Claude Code, Antigravity; label Gemini only as legacy where retained.

preMortem.scenario: Legacy Gemini compatibility is accidentally broken
preMortem.trigger: Removing or renaming gemini host id in persisted records or fallbacks
preMortem.consequence: Older dispatch records, policies, or tests fail unexpectedly
preMortem.mitigation: Keep gemini accepted as deprecated legacy in runtime normalization and add verification for legacy probe/list behavior.

preMortem.scenario: Unattended safety becomes overstated for Antigravity
preMortem.trigger: Copying Codex/Gemini live dispatch support without checking agy semantics
preMortem.consequence: Lattice claims a stronger host capability than verified
preMortem.mitigation: Keep noninteractive/live-dispatch claims conservative unless code already proves bounded agy invocation; probe should report availability without claiming production authority.
